messages.text: Hearn: Talks 'reopened' for Fury vs AJ at Wembley

metadata.summary: Promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have "reopened" to stage the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium.
metadata.content: Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn says talks have 'reopened' to stage British heavyweight blockbuster at Wembley Stadium | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Breaking Fury vs Joshua: Eddie Hearn says talks have 'reopened' to stage British heavyweight blockbuster at Wembley Stadium A long-awaited blockbuster fight between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury has been stuck in negotiations in recent months amid an apparent disagreement over the location for the event, Joshua's team having remained insistent it must take place in the United Kingdom Friday 4 September 2026 15:20, UK Image: Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury could finally settle their rivalry at Wembley Stadium Promoter Eddie Hearn has announced that talks have "reopened" to stage the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium. Negotiations for the Fury vs Joshua fight had hit a major stumbling block after Madison Square Garden in New York emerged as the preferred venue to stage the blockbuster bout. But Hearn has released a statement on social media, revealing that Wembley is again being considered as the venue for the fight. He wrote: "I want to thank everyone for the unbelievable support!" "You have been heard and talks have now re-opened for Wembley. "Let's make history with one of the biggest sporting moments (British flag) has ever seen." messages.text: Arrow gets emotional farewell on 100th Rabbitohs appearance after MND diagnosis

metadata.summary: Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis.
metadata.content: Jai Arrow gets emotional farewell 100th NRL appearance for South Sydney Rabbitohs after Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to content Jai Arrow gets emotional farewell 100th NRL appearance for South Sydney Rabbitohs after Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis Jai Arrow retired from rugby league in May following an MND diagnosis; NRL gave South Sydney Rabbitohs special dispensation to include Arrow in their squad and feature as an extra player for the last two matches of the regular season, allowing him to pass 100 appearances for the club Friday 4 September 2026 14:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player South Sydney Rabbitohs player Jai Arrow receives an emotional welcome as he leads out the side for the last time after his MND diagnosis Jai Arrow made an emotional 100th NRL appearance for the South Sydney Rabbitohs to mark his farewell from the sport, following his Motor Neurone Disease diagnosis. Special dispensation had been granted by the NRL and Rabbitohs to allow Arrow the opportunity to take to the field for the opening kick-off another two times, with the game against Sydney Roosters marking a century of appearances. Arrow walked his team out onto the field for the Sydney derby, with 'Stand By Me' playing before 'You'll Never Walk Alone' then rang around the Allianz Stadium. messages.text: Leclerc leads Hamilton as Ferrari seal practice one-two after upgrades

metadata.summary: Charles Leclerc led a one-two from team-mate Lewis Hamilton in Italian Grand Prix first practice as Ferrari impressed after debuting an engine upgrade at Monza.
metadata.content: Italian GP: Charles Leclerc leads Lewis Hamilton as Ferrari seal one-two in first Monza practice after revealing upgrades | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Italian GP: Charles Leclerc leads Lewis Hamilton as Ferrari seal one-two in first Monza practice after revealing upgrades Charles Leclerc leads Ferrari one-two from Lewis Hamilton in first practice; Ferrari impress after unveiling latest upgrades for home race; watch Friday's second practice session for the Italian GP at 3pm, live on Sky Sports F1; Qualifying is at 3pm on Saturday Friday 4 September 2026 14:52, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Ted Kravitz takes a closer look at Ferrari’s major upgrades as they go all-in for their home Italian Grand Prix at Monza. Charles Leclerc led a one-two from team-mate Lewis Hamilton in Italian Grand Prix first practice as Ferrari impressed after debuting an engine upgrade at Monza. Leclerc's time of 1:23.008s put him 0.173s clear of Hamilton, with Mercedes' George Russell a further tenth back in third. World championship leader Kimi Antonelli, who will start from the back of the grid in Sunday's race after exceeding his allowance of engine parts for the season, was fifth for Mercedes. messages.text: Big Mojo fancied to return Sprint Cup crown

metadata.summary: Kate Tracey was joined by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix to preview another busy weekend of action, which includes the Group 1 Sprint Cup from Haydock.
metadata.content: Haydock tips: Big Mojo fancied to retain Sprint Cup crown | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Haydock tips: Big Mojo fancied to retain Sprint Cup crown Ahead of another busy Saturday of action, Kate Tracey is joined on the Weekend Winners panel by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix; in this week's episode, the team take aim at Haydock, paying particular attention to the feature Sprint Cup Friday 4 September 2026 12:11, UK Image: Kate Tracey is joined by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix on Weekend Winners Kate Tracey was joined by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix to preview another busy weekend of action, which includes the Group 1 Sprint Cup from Haydock. Eight runners are set to go in challenging conditions, with the ground expected to be heavy for this six-furlong dash. Almeraq heads the market as he aims to bounce back from disappointment in the July Cup, while Wathnan duo Kind Of Blue and Paborus also take their chance. Marvelman and Coppull represent Andrew Balding and Clive Cox respectively, and last year's winner Big Mojo returns to defend his crown. Declan Rix… "I'm with the favourite Almeraq . He's a wonderful horse who I think deserves an awful lot of credit after that horror fall he took at York - it was a proper mother-and-a-father fall. To come back and win on his first start in the Cathedral Stakes, it was like someone had said a prayer for him.
